title: Architecture
description: How AskDocuMind is put together: where a request goes, how a document becomes searchable, and how an answer is built. Each diagram covers one part of the system.

sections.name: System overview
sections.description: The Next.js client on Vercel reaches the FastAPI API on Railway through Cloudflare. The API uses Postgres with pgvector on Neon, an S3-compatible bucket, OpenAI and Brave Search, and runs ingestion, the upload sweeper and user cleanup as background tasks in the same process.

sections.name: RAG pipeline
sections.description: The question is rewritten by gpt-4o-mini, embedded, and matched against this chat’s chunks in pgvector. If fewer than 3 match and web search is on, Brave Search adds up to 5 pages. A cross-encoder reranks the results, and the top 15 go to gpt-4o-mini to write the answer.

sections.name: Upload handling
sections.description: Uploads are validated, saved to object storage and acknowledged with a 202. A background task, up to 5 at once, extracts, chunks and embeds the text, while a sweeper retries or fails stuck uploads every 60 seconds.

sections.name: Data models
sections.description: Five tables: users, chat sessions, chat messages, documents and chunk embeddings, all with cascading deletes. Each chunk stores a 1536-dimension vector and its chat ID, so searches stay within one chat.
